turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor:
Hi! Let's do one example together first.
I work on Mondays. He works on Mondays.
Step 1: find the person: "he".
Step 2: he, she or it means one other person or thing, so add -s: works.
Rule: after he, she or it, put -s on the verb.
Right: She works at a shop. Wrong: She work at a shop.

Now you try. Write the verb only:
Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)
